notes.content:
[url=https://youtu.be/ZvDW-NTQjFw][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/24570646/ae77136e8f8fa09fc2c0df8f4f1eadb00413fc9d.png[/img][/url]

Greetings, Hot Lava fans! We can’t wait for you to jump in to our newest update featuring:

[h1]BRAND NEW CHARACTERS![/h1]
Get ready for a new in-game toy universe EXO-CLASH!. Set in another galaxy where giant robots fight colossal monsters. Captain Hera Scarlet and Lt Leo Satomi have landed in the game complete with their own unique unlockable items, taunts, and Action Files.

[h1]NEW WEEKLY MODE![/h1]
There’s now even more reason to jump into Hot Lava regularly with the weekly course. Compete with others for top global positions on a new course and ability each week. Earn a reward for placing on the leaderboard then try again when it cycles to a new course each Tuesday.

[h1]SUMMER ACTIVITIES![/h1]
Splash into summer with water balloons and more when you visit the Playground in the next few weeks. Challenge someone to a water balloon fight, or hit all the targets around the level for your chance at earning a reward. These activities will only be around during summer so hit your mark while you can!

You can enjoy all the features of this dynamic new update right now. Meanwhile, we’ll keep working on ways to make our game even hotter. So stay tuned, stay cool and stay off the floor!

[list]
[*]Beat the weekly course and earn a reward
[*]Play as Hera or Leo from the Exo-Clash universe
[*]Throwable water balloons now available in Playground Level
[*]Hit all the targets to earn a cool new accessory
[*]Checkpoints added to Chase Your Sister courses
[*]Level up faster with increased XP gains across the board

notes.title: It's Klei Fest! - Updates and Announcements For All Things Klei!
notes.content:
Hey Everybody!

It’s time for our big [url=https://store.steampowered.com/sale/kleifest]annual publisher sale[/url] on Steam!

During Klei Fest, we’ll have a big burst of content, items, events, sales and interesting stuff happening for all things Klei! And this year’s fest is bigger than ever.

Of course with a new map and characters we have two new courses, and plenty of new collectables and accessories!

Greetings Hot Lava fans! As the weather heats up, so does your favorite game with a brand-spanking new update to warm your heart. 

[h3]BRAND! NEW! MAP![/h3]
Hold onto your pizza slices, it’s a brand new Klei created map! Rocco’s Arcade is a hotbed of hopping set in a retro-arcade pizza place. Check out two new courses! Take on the pogo and tiny toy trials! Interact with gobs of retro-games like Flamly Ball, Zeet-ball and Thump-a-Raccoon! 

[h3]TWO NEW CHARACTERS[/h3]
Say hello to two new characters: T. Rex and Venomess - two rocking reptilian members of Mutant Mayhem! Select them on the character screen and level them up to unlock a cavalcade of new collectables!
[h3]
NEW ITEMS [/h3]
On top of all the awesome items you can get leveling up the characters, we also have a handful of bonus cool collectable sets of accessories. The more you play, the more you collect, so jump back in and check out all the new stuff. We have plenty of daily challenges and plenty of online opponents to race against. See you all there!

As always, stay cool, stay safe and stay off the floor!

notes.title: Hot Lava Journey Update Now Live!
notes.content:
[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1TezogSfvh4][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/24570646/120a29d1a76aa540c793c552dab7cc804360eb89.png[/img][/url]
[h2]AWESOME AUGUST UPDATE[/h2]
Hello Hot Lava fans! August is here and we’re bringing the heat for the final days of summer with a scorching new update!
[h2]DAILY CHALLENGES[/h2]
New ‘Daily Challenges’ give you even more reason to jump into Hot Lava on the regular. New rewards are up for grabs - Every. Single. Day. Complete the challenges for some fantastic daily rewards. If you get doubles, don’t fret, we’ve got an exciting new system that addresses that...

notes.content:
Originally posted by [url=https://forums.kleientertainment.com/forums/topic/123309-hot-lava-roadmap/]DanaS on the official forums[/url]:

It has been just over a year since Hot Lava launched on Steam and Apple Arcade and we wanted to check in with our amazing fans to say thanks and update everyone about some of the exciting things we have planned for the future.

[h2]Previously on… Hot Lava[/h2]

Our fantastic fan base was instrumental and inspirational in aiding the team to polish Hot Lava through the thrilling beta phase of development. Their heroic feedback pushed the boundaries of what this game could be and epically cheered us on as we equipped Hot Lava with bigger and better challenges. We cannot stress enough how crucial our fans were in this truly transformative time.

Along with our monumental release, a thrilling new audience appeared thanks to Apple Arcade! This new audience showed us that people were just as enthusiastic about jumping around in molten hot environments on mobile as on PC. 

Over the past year we’ve been pummeled with a lot of positive feedback and some sensational suggestions about how to make Hot Lava more accessible to newer players and to seasoned pros.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/24570646/23b52cc3b5934c190b5d5548d58329aa6dddcba6.jpg[/img]

[h2]And now...[/h2]

Our newest update introduced two T.O.X.I.C. new characters -- Lord Sludge and Poizone -- armed with two new movesets. Poizone’s double jump gives players a way to leap to some hard to reach spots and Lord Sludge’s slide moves provide an alternative to hitting those higher speeds previously only achievable by mastering our boost system.

Teaming up with these new characters is our amazing new progression system that introduced a whole new set of rewards: sensational new skins and character-specific items that are unlocked when players level-up their character and awesome new Action Files to fill you in on lots of G.A.T. and T.O.X.I.C. trivia.

Apple Arcade users with LiDAR-equipped devices also got an added treat in Hot Lava’s incredible new AR feature. Finally, people at home can enjoy the fun of having molten hot lava fill their living room without all the messy clean up.

We’ve gotten some great feedback on these new features, including suggestions on what you want to see. So, on that note, we’d like to let you in on what we have planned for Hot Lava: Year 2.

[h2]Next Time on Hot Lava...[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/24570646/cd5ef0fa1f064d3f4f3b25207463b3ded71fb61f.jpg[/img]
[h2]Jen Forcer’s Tactical Training Updates[/h2]

Our mission moving forward is to make the game more accessible to newer players while still challenging veteran players with four phases of fantastic updates we’re calling ‘[b]Jen Forcer’s Tactical Training Updates[/b]’ periodically deploying throughout the coming year. Updates that fall under a few categories:

[h2]Menu and Early Course Overhaul[/h2]
We’re on a mission to improve our user experience. It’s our duty to leave no Hot Lava player behind, whether they’re hardcore veteran players or rookies who just jumped in. With this in mind we’ll be shining up and shipping out improvements to our menu system. Things like making it more apparent where your items and unlockables are and implementing a replay saving system that will bring videos of your runs front and center so they’re easier to locate.

Some of our early courses will also see some improvements throughout the year to make it easier for first time players, yet still challenging to those who want to push themselves to be the best that they can be.

[h2]New Characters[/h2]
Lord Sludge and Poizone were just the first in a slew of new characters we plan to unleash. While our lips are sealed on which characters are coming up and when, rest assured that some long rumored appearances from figures outside of the GAT universe have set their sights on future invasions.  

[h2]New (non-Canon) Levels[/h2]
A brand new level made by one of our collaborators will arrive this winter, and with it will be some exciting new exclusive items to unlock. We also have an arsenal of community maps from our awesome modding community which we will deploy for future fun.

[h2]New Items, New Skins, New Content[/h2]
Keep a lookout for new content including items and skins and videos for everyone to enjoy. We’re hard at work making new content for the game and calculating ways to improve what we have.

As always we want you to send us feedback. So sign into the forums and let us know how we’re doing. We always read what you post and always look forward to dispatches from the field.

You are going to be playing a series of new worlds, Playground, Wholesale and Mastery that were added during the Beta, as well as a brand new world called “Basement” launching today. Our item system has moved away from randomized drops and towards a purely progression based unlock system. Mechanics have been refined over numerous iterations to create an incredibly deep player controller. We have also added full controller support, optimized performance and translated the game into 15 languages. But we still have so many exciting updates we can’t wait to share with you.

notes.title: Hot Lava, Klei's sizzling parkour game, is arriving next week
notes.content:
After a year in open beta, Hot Lava is almost ready for release. With Oxygen Not Included appearing in July, along with the Early Access launch of Griftlands, I confess I'd forgotten all about Klei's first-person parkour game, despite its abundance of personality. To mark the impending launch, you can watch another brief episode of Global Action Heroes, Klei's homage to cartoons like G.I. Joe. 

In Hot Lava, you'll be playing as toys based on the fictional cartoon. Thankfully, they're all poseable action figures with the necessary agility to navigate an obstacle course that's bathed in lava. The game's worlds are all mundane rooms, from a high school gym to a hideous '80s living room, but they've all been turned into deadly molten swimming pools. 

Navigating these treacherous museums of nostalgia requires a lot of jumping, swinging and, apparently, surfing. You can play with up to eight friends, too, competing with them for a coveted spot on the leaderboard. Once you've mastered the courses, you might want to check out what other players have created. Hot Lava comes with a Unity level construction kit and already has Steam Workshop support.

The launch update will introduce a basement level, a new progression system that replaces randomised drops, improvements to controls and performance, and more. There are no patch notes yet, however, so we'll have to wait to see the full extent of the jump to 1.0.  

Hot Lava is due out on September 19, and Klei says it will continue to update the game with new stuff, tweaks and bug fixes after launch.

When we launch into release many aspects of the game will have a fresh start. Our levels and player mechanics have been growing and changing over this beta so much that we will reset all leaderboards. Inventories and progress will be incompatible with our new systems.

Those who have helped us test during this beta phase will be rewarded with a very special unique item to say “thank you”.

On that note, THANK YOU! The feedback, bug reports, and custom levels we have received from this community has been insanely influential to the development of this game. We could not have gotten here without you, and I can’t wait to show you what we have been working on for launch.

I want to once again thank everyone for all the love and support you have shown over the open beta phase, and I can’t wait to show you what we are working on next!

notes.title: Community Update
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/KO1J4P8.gif[/img]
[i]Hazard modeling the new football item set[/i]

As we are working hard on preparing Hot Lava for Early Access, I wanted to take some time to talk about some amazing things going on in the Hot Lava community.

[h1]Translations[/h1]
Yesterday we added support for user created translations of Hot Lava, and in under 24 hours we have seen 'Russian', 'Spanish', 'Turkish' and even 'Pirate' translation mods appear on the workshop! If you are interested in helping translate Hot Lava to another language, details can be found on the [url=https://forums.kleientertainment.com/forums/topic/95685-creatingusing-language-translations/]Klei forums[/url].  To view translations as they are added [url=https://steamcommunity.com/workshop/browse/?appid=382560&browsesort=trend&section=readytouseitems&admin_view=1&requiredtags%5B0%5D=Language&actualsort=trend&p=1&days=-1]visit the workshop[/url]

[h1]Custom Levels[/h1]
Through the Community Spotlight we have been highlighting some of the best and most accessible levels the community has been producing.  But please know this is just the tip of the iceberg- the workshop is littered with plenty of other creative, surprising, and challenging maps!
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/workshop/browse/?appid=382560&browsesort=trend&section=readytouseitems&admin_view=1&requiredtags%5B0%5D=Level&actualsort=trend&p=1&days=90]View workshop maps[/url]

[h1]Modkit Update[/h1]
The Modkit is being updated today.  Support for multi-course levels,  game modes (like pogo), consistent export names (only retire leaderboard when you intend to), modkit friendly wall jumps and much more!  It's strongly recommended that you install the modkit to a new project and port existing maps over to avoid corruption. We will continue to build on and improve the Modkit based on your feedback.  The new modkit should go live in the next hour.

[h1]Community Tournament[/h1]
The speed running community for Hot Lava has become very competitive.  Many world records have been secured by fractions of a second.  A "Full School Run" tournament will be happening on the 22nd at 11am PST, 2pm EST,  7pm CET.  The competition will be streamed on [url=https://www.twitch.tv/dawnfinder]Twitch[/url].  If you think you have what it takes and want to sign up,  or are just interested in following the competitive scene an [url=https://discord.gg/ssCxKYu]event discord has been setup[/url].

[h1]Award Items[/h1] 
To show our appreciation towards the community we have added two award items.  The Wrench and Crown.  These items will be awarded for recipients of the Community Spotlight and the to the winners of select Community Competitions respectively.  Those who were featured in previous spotlights have retroactively received this award. Thank you for helping grow Hot Lava through your contributions!
[img]https://i.imgur.com/f5xBPvk.gif[/img]

[h1]Developer Stream[/h1]
Klei hosts a weekly developer stream where we talk about on of our games- and this week (like, right now) you can catch us talking about Hot Lava.  More details are available on the [url=https://forums.kleientertainment.com/forums/topic/95706-rhymes-with-play-hot-lava-update-dev-stream/]Klei forums[/url].

[h1]Hot Lava Discord[/h1]
If you are interested in becoming involved in any part of the Hot Lava community- or just want a chill place to hang out, please join me on the [url=https://discord.gg/RXDfHV4]Hot Lava Discord[/url].

notes.title: The floor is literally lava in the beta of Klei's energetic first-person platformer
notes.content:
In some respects you've already played Klei Entertainment's new first-person parkour platformer. As a kid you pretended the floor was lava, maybe in your bedroom or living room, and tried to get from one side of the room to the other without touching the carpet until a parent yelled at you. "Knock it off! Don't stand on that! Go play outside!"

As a kid in Hot Lava, which is now in open beta (it'll enter Early Access later) you're inspired by a superhero cartoon you see on TV. It's quite a good one, complete with the hero whose swimming powers don't come in handy due to the lack of an ocean (plus she can't even understand her own dolphin). Watching the heroes battle a dastardly lava boss captures your imagination, and that makes just getting upstairs and into bed a daring adventure. The carpet turns to lava and you parkour off furniture and walls and swing from the chandelier.

At school, the fantasy continues with your classmates—in this case, other players—as you bounce around the hallways, classrooms, gym, and cafeteria, being sure to never touch the floor.

There are a number of parkour moves beyond simply jumping. Keep an eye out for items outlined in green, like ropes and platforms, since they can be grabbed with a mouse-click and swung from, or sometimes even clambered onto. Green smears on vertical surfaces indicate wall running is possible by sticking to the glop and propelling yourself forward. You can boost your speed, and thus the length of your jumps by strafing and rotating in the same direction while jumping, and surf along certain objects as though railsliding without a skateboard.

As you're bouncing around you can collect cards that unlock new cosmetic customization options for your character. Plus, you can see how you fared against your Steam friends in timed challenges with a leaderboard. I also saw a player bouncing around with a pogo stick that I now desperately want.

One big issue I've been having in the beta is with unstable frame rates. The first time I played on Wednesday I would abruptly drop from around 60 fps to single digits—which isn't great when you're trying to time jumps or grab ropes. I played again this morning and it was considerably smoother, but there are still occasional drops in fps that threw off my timing.

First-person parkour is tricky to pull off in a game, especially on keyboard and mouse, and really needs a natural fluidity as you speed through jumps and activate movement skills. In that respect, Hot Lava isn't really there yet. Again, it's in beta, but at this early stage it's lacking a certain smoothness to its movement. It's still good fun to play, and the art, character animation, and environments are wonderful, too. But there's plenty more work to be done before it really makes me feels like a kid imagining himself being a parkour superhero, instead of an adult trying to imagine himself being a kid.

notes.title: Klei quietly began the open beta for Hot Lava during E3
notes.content:
The trailer for Hot Lava is something else. It's a five-minute homage to Saturday morning cartoons complete with theme song and an ad break for "the Mount Vile Gauntlet Trial playset". The actual game it's a trailer for is, like that playset, an elaborate obstacle course where—just like we pretended as kids—the floor is lava.

Hot Lava is what Klei have been working on alongside Oxygen is Not Included and new DLC for Don't Starve. In the middle of E3 fever during the week, they quietly launched it into open beta on Steam, meaning that you can play it right now.

They've clarified that this is not part of Steam's Early Access program, however. When games go into Early Access they get a chance to be featured on the front page, go into the recommendations algorithm, become eligible for user review, and generally become a part of the greater Steam ecosystem. Klei don't want this version of Hot Lava to go through all of that. They've had open betas available through their website before, and did something similarly stealthy for Oxygen Not Included. It means Hot Lava will be available on Steam without being visible to people who aren't specifically looking for it.

Apparently the plan is for an Early Access release to follow when Hot Lava's ready for it, but if you want to get in earlier than Early, here's the Steam page.

notes.title: Note about "Open Beta"
notes.content:
Hey everybody. 

There has been some confusion regarding "Open Beta". So I thought I would take a moment to clarify. 

In the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/382560/announcements/detail/1660020759111211179]open beta announcement[/url] we said: [quote]We're not quite ready for the massive rush of early-access yet. When a game goes into early-access it becomes part of the entire Steam ecosystem with curators, reviews, banner rotations and top sellers lists. So we're keeping a low profile for now until we believe we are ready for early-access. "[/quote] 

When a game goes into early access, it is then part of steam. So it will suggest the game to people who like that sort of game or games your friends are playing. It appears in top sellers lists, it's open for reviews, Steam recommends it to your friends and basically the game is given a soft marketing push by Steam. We don't want this right now. However, we have a lot of people who want to play the game. So. We're doing an open beta. 

Basically, we want to sell the game through steam to people who know about it, but we don't want steam to help people find it.

This is the same thing we have done for Don't Starve, Don't Starve Together, Invisible Inc and most recently Oxygen Not Included. However, previously we sold keys to be redeemed in Steam through our website- beginning with Oxygen Not Included we can sell directly through Steam Thanks to Valve.

We put a banner up on the store page so it was super clear that the game is in Open Beta - hopefully Steam will have better messaging for this in the future like they do for Early-Access.

We realize this was confusing, and we appologize. Last time we did this for Oxygen Not Included you couldn't even search for the game on steam and you could only get it through a special link... THAT was confusing. 

Sorry for the mix up. We'll see what we can do to clarify that directly on the store page.  

Thanks everybody. 

EDIT: (Thanks for the questions)

Closed Beta - Invite only. If you didn't sign up in time, you couldn't play. 
Open Beta - Anybody can purchase the game and play. 

I understand that some games use a free open beta to stress test their servers before they launch, and I apologize that I did not realize there would be confusion there. 

Additionally, if you played during closed beta, we let players keep the game, for free. No need to pay for the game again. Ever. 

Anybody who buys the game now or in the future keeps the game including people who were given the game for free or were gifted by friends. 

Hopefully that clears it all up. Once again, thanks for the feedback and support.

notes.title: First-person platformer Hot Lava launches bring a pal
notes.content:
It’s a risky gambit to launch an offbeat little game in the middle of the E3 hype-storm, but Klei Entertainment just love danger if Hot Lava is any indication. It’s a first-person platformer starring a cast of highly meltable plastic action figures, navigating a human-scale world where every child’s playtime nightmare has come to pass: the floor is lava. Today, it launches (as an open beta) at a discounted price, and every copy includes a second to share with a friend. Hopping between furniture isn’t as much fun without someone to confirm your falls, after all.

notes.title: Hot Lava is a first-person parkour-survival game from the maker of Don't Starve
notes.content:
Klei Interactive, the maker of Mark of the Ninja, Don't Starve, and Invisible Inc., is working on a new game, which also happens to be its first-ever 3D game, called Hot Lava. The idea behind it actually comes from a very old game that you may have played as a child: The floor is made of molten lava, and if you step on it, you die!

The floor is literally made of lava in hot lava, although it doesn't appear to melt the laundry basket or set fire to the teacher's desk. There's also a lot more Mirror's Edge to it than the couch-to-coffee-table clambering of childhood, and sliding on frictionless surfaces will allow you to to reach incredible speeds and perform impossible jumps. The adventure will unfold across distinct worlds, from school hallways to the memories of your darkest fears, and it will also, according to the Steam page, support some form of multiplayer.

The system requirements are listed too, but they're so low as to be almost irrelevant: Windows 7, 2GB RAM, DirectX 9.0, and 5GB of drive space. A launch date hasn't been announced, but Klei is now taking signups for a closed beta at playhotlava.com.

Thanks, GamesRadar.
